summary: THE DUNGEON MOVEMENT KEYS ARE THE ARROW KEYS, and they work in the harness. Live before/after deltas on the committed corridor state (base 0xffa0): key 'left' -> facing 0->3 (turn left, -1 mod 4); key 'right' -> facing 0->1 (turn right, +1 mod 4); key 'up' -> step forward (x 5->6, gy 121->122, facing unchanged). Each turn AND a forward step REBUILDS the span list (@0x50ce/0x50d0) and REDRAWS the 3D viewport (turn = ~11700 changed pixels out of the 176x112 viewport; parity bit @0x521a flips 0->1). All four facings are reachable (left cycles 0->3->2->1->0; right cycles 0->1->2->3->0). THE 'BOXED AT THE GATE' ROOT CAUSE was TWO compounding things, NEITHER of which is a broken arrow key: (1) the prior `reach` recipe used ENTER for 'forward' — but ENTER = the on-screen 'PRESS RETURN FOR OPTIONS' = the main-menu/camp trigger, NOT a move; the apparent forward progress in `reach` was ENTER repeatedly dismissing the entry narration. Turns were never tried with the arrows. (2) The committed corridor frame sits in a 3-CELL DEAD-END STUB (gx fixed 127; cells x=5<->6<->7 along the axis, walls on both ends and the sides): from x=5 forward reaches x=7 then stops (the gate/front wall at x=8); the cell behind x=5 is also a wall. So `up` only moves twice before the wall-collision gate (maze_can_step_in_facing 0x3244 returns 1=blocked) makes it a no-op — which LOOKS like 'boxed' if you don't turn. TURNING and the available forward steps both rebuild the span list, which is exactly what the renderer validation needs. SECONDARY FINDING: the DOWN arrow is NOT a back-step in the Wiz6 dungeon view (it is a no-op even when the cell directly behind is OPEN — verified from the far end x=7 with x=6 open behind). The on-screen widget only offers up (forward) + left/right (turn); to reverse, turn 180 (right x2) then step forward (verified: x6 facing0 -> 180 -> facing2 -> up -> x5). A turned-around frame (facing 2) yields a 4-span looking-back view — a richer multi-wall variant for renderer validation. CAVEAT on the prior finding: the maze-span-build.json claim 'Arrow-key turns still do NOT register in this harness (no turn key found)' and 'the party is boxed at the gate (gy 118->119 on first step, then all keys are no-ops; facing never changes)' is WRONG for the committed corridor state — arrows register and turns change facing through all 4 values. That earlier negative was almost certainly observed against the fresh `reach`-driven state immediately after the entry narration, where input is briefly modal, rather than the settled corridor fixture.

findings.claim: The dungeon movement keys are the arrow keys, and they register in the dosbox-pure harness. left/right turn (facing -/+1 mod 4); up steps forward when the cell ahead is open. Each turn and each successful forward step rebuilds the span list (@0x50ce count / 0x50d0 list) and redraws the 3D viewport (parity @0x521a flips).

evidence.details: Live deltas on tools/libretro/states/maze-corridor.state (base 0xffa0), one fresh restore per key, read DGROUP facing 0x4f9a / x 0x4f9e / gx 0x4fa4 / gy 0x4fa2 / parity 0x521a / span-count 0x50ce: key 'left' -> facing 0->3, parity 0->1, spans 1->0; key 'right' -> facing 0->1, parity 0->1, spans 1->0; key 'up' -> x 5->6, gy 121->122, facing 0, parity 0->1, spans 1->0. 4x 'left' cycles facing 0->3->2->1->0; 4x 'right' cycles 0->1->2->3->0. Viewport (x72..247/y32..143) pixel diff vs the clean frame: turn-left 11743 px, turn-right 11697 px (a full wall-geometry change). Screenshots /tmp/turn-base.png (wall+doorway), /tmp/turn-left.png (open corridor) are unmistakable Wiz6 3D dungeon views with the on-screen 'TURN <-/->' + '^' widget. Reproduce: `pnpm tsx tools/libretro/trace-maze.ts move`.

findings.claim: The 'boxed at the gate' behavior was NOT a broken arrow key. Root cause is two compounding things: (1) the committed corridor frame is in a 3-cell dead-end stub (gx fixed 127; cells x=5<->6<->7, walls on both ends + sides) so the forward step (up) only moves twice (x5->6->7) before the wall-collision gate makes it a no-op; (2) the prior `reach` recipe used ENTER for 'forward', but ENTER = the on-screen 'PRESS RETURN FOR OPTIONS' (camp/main-menu) — a non-move — and turns were never attempted with the arrow keys.

evidence.details: Live: from x=5 facing0, `up` gives x5->6->7 then stops (3rd up = no change). Turn 180 (right x2 -> facing2) then `up` returns x6->5 (so the wall is at x=8 ahead and x=4 behind — a stub). `down` is a no-op everywhere incl. from x=7 with x=6 open behind. Static: maze_can_step_in_facing (wmaze 0x3244) pushes (gy,gx,x,y[0x4fa0],z[0x4f9c],facing) and calls maze_check_wall_in_direction (0xf2a) + maze_can_pass_doors_and_walls (0x309d); `cmp ax,2; jge 0x3281; ...; 0x3281 mov ax,1` -> returns 1 (blocked) when a wall is present, which gates the step into a no-op. The turn handler maze_rotate_party (0x3304, called @ wmaze 0x21) increments facing 0x4f9a by 1 mod 4 then re-renders + polls — no wall gate, so a turn ALWAYS succeeds + redraws.

findings.claim: The DOWN arrow is not a step-backward in the Wiz6 dungeon view; it is a no-op. The Wiz6 movement model has no back-step — the on-screen widget offers only forward (up) + turn (left/right). Reversing is done by turning 180 then stepping forward.

evidence.details: Live: walked to the far end (x=7, gy=123) where x=6 is open directly behind, then `down` x2 -> NO change (x stays 7). From x=5, `down` -> no change. Contrast: 180-turn (right x2 -> facing2) then `up` -> x6->5 reliably reverses. So 'down' is dead in this view; back-tracking is turn-180+forward. The reverse demo also yields a facing-2 frame with a 4-span looking-back view (a multi-wall variant).
